components: The first year consists of ten compulsory 6-EC courses. Completing all 60 EC meets the first-year continuation threshold of 54 EC. What You Don’t Learn in School is an additional non-credit requirement in Years 1 and 2.
Economics for a Changing World I
Law and Behaviour requires the first-year Law, Justice and Morality course.
Economics for a Changing World II
Economics for a Changing World II requires Economics for a Changing World I.
Politics, Power and Governance II requires the first-year course. Its content centres on European integration, EU institutions and contemporary crises.
The Politics major requires Politics, Power and Governance I. The listed Politics courses form one major; courses from the other three majors are not added.
Skills and Research Methods for Political Science
The methods course develops quantitative political analysis and qualitative inquiry. Prior Introduction to Statistical Analysis is recommended and is completed in Year 1.
Conflict and Cooperation in Global Politics
Psychology and Society II requires Psychology and Society I. The course examines cultural and cross-cultural psychology.

Research Lab develops an interdisciplinary research proposal and offers methodological tutorial tracks. It is a separate compulsory course from the thesis; prior research-methods study is recommended.

The 12-EC thesis is an individual interdisciplinary research report, with an oral defence, in the second semester of Year 3. Entry requires 120 EC from academic core or major courses before that semester; electives do not count. Completing Years 1 and 2 and the first-semester major courses meets this threshold.

Twelve EC remain for electives, normally in the first semester of Year 3. Courses outside the designated PPLE electives require Examinations Board approval. An approved 6- or 12-EC internship may use this space; no internship or particular elective is assumed.
formalSections: TER B-3.2–3.4, pp. 19–20: shared core and Politics major
TER B-3.5–3.8, pp. 21–23: thesis, electives, course sequence
findings: The public programme is English-taught, honours and interdisciplinary. Its public course-catalogue link leads to 2024, so the dated 2026 programme page 41161 and adopted 2026–2027 TER were retrieved through official alternatives. The public aggregate 102/66/12 is correct but unsuitable as the only comparison detail: replaced it with 27 named courses and 12 elective credits. No core/major parent is added to its children.

TER B-3.2 lists ten compulsory first-year courses of six EC, totalling sixty, followed by five shared core courses in Year 2 and two in Year 3: 102 core EC. B-3.4 lists Politics first among four majors. Retained Politics before UCR selection, counting its five Year-2 courses, four Year-3 courses and twelve-credit thesis: 66 EC. Psychology, Law and Economics/Business paths are mutually exclusive and not summed into the route. Catalogue aggregate totals across all paths are not degree-year totals.

Year 2 combines thirty core and thirty Politics credits. Year 3 combines eighteen Politics taught credits, twelve core credits, a twelve-credit thesis and twelve open credits. In Semester 1 Authority/Accountability and Political Economy occupy block 1, Politics of the Present block 2, and electives blocks 2/3. Psychology and Society II plus Research Lab are in block 4, Political Behaviour in block 5, and the thesis in blocks 5/6. Each year and semester closes without adding resits, aliases or parallel majors.

Law and Behaviour requires Law, Justice and Morality (called LJM I in the course entry). Economics for a Changing World II requires I; Politics, Power and Governance II requires I; Psychology and Society II requires I. Politics-major entry requires Politics, Power and Governance I. All are completed in Year 1 before dependent work. Statistical Analysis precedes the recommended political-methods foundation; all earlier methods precede Research Lab. The Economics/Business mathematics test does not apply to the selected Politics major.

The first-year sixty-credit completion meets the 54-EC positive-continuation rule in TER A-4.3a. The non-credit What You Don’t Learn in School programme is retained separately for Years 1 and 2. Research Lab is a proposal/design course, not an alternative name for the thesis. The thesis is an individual 8,000–10,000-word report integrating at least two disciplines with mandatory oral presentation/defence. TER B-3.8 and the dated thesis entry require 120 EC excluding electives before its semester. Completing both earlier years supplies these credits; first-semester Year-3 major work supplies additional headroom.

TER B-3.6 preserves twelve elective EC: outside-designated PPLE electives require Examinations Board approval. An approved six- or twelve-credit internship can use the window, but no internship, external course or host is instantiated. The catalogue designated-electives group is not an additional compulsory group and is not added to open credits.

Course contents support social/behavioural psychology, normative law and ethics, economic decision-making, macroeconomics, EU integration, political theory, democracy, international relations, public policy, empirical methods and interdisciplinary work. The 2026 Politics of the Present specifically examines democracy/truth/media; Psychology and Society II is cultural and cross-cultural psychology. These detailed contents control partial UCR relationships and deliberate gaps, rather than either identical-credit demands or title-only pairing.
